why: rcl selects WHICH event with an enum passed to a generic `rcl_publisher_event_init` / `rcl_subscription_event_init`. Ours has one named registration function per event (`rclc_publisher_set_liveliness_lost_callback` and friends, classified in the pubsub stage), so the enum has no argument position to appear in and each callback can carry its own typed payload instead of a `void *`. rcl makes a QoS event a first-class OBJECT: `rcl_event_t` is initialised from an entity plus an event-type enum, added to a wait set, and drained with `rcl_take_event`. Ours registers a typed callback per event directly on the entity, so there is no event handle to zero-initialise, validate, add to a set or finalise. Constraints: no allocator for the `rcl_event_impl_t` the handle hides, and RFC-0002's executor drives entities through the RMW vtable with no wait set for an event to join. Same decision the pubsub stage recorded for the callbacks themselves -- see `cpp:QOSEventHandler`. Separately, both rcl enums include `*_INCOMPATIBLE_QOS`, which we do not raise -- see `cpp:QOSOfferedIncompatibleQoSInfo`.
